$comment: SOURCE, NOT GENERATED. Hand-written notes for the changelog, keyed by version, plus `unreleased` for work that has no version yet. Everything else on that page is derived from git, which is the right way round for drawings: a list of what was added or redrawn should never be typed. A release is not always drawings, though. The corner treatment added a whole axis without adding a name, so git had nothing to report and the page announced 48 redraws and nothing else. Write a note only where the release did something a count cannot describe, lead with what changed and how much, and keep it to two sentences: this sits above the tiles, not instead of them. Numbers go in as {names} and {files} and are counted at build, because a typed number is a claim with an expiry date and this repository has already shipped three of them. Plain prose, since neither the page nor the Paper board renders markdown. Entries are never edited once published, for the reason pipeline/README.md gives about the changelog only ever growing.
0.3.0: Sharp corners, across the whole set: {files} SVGs now, against {names} names, because every drawing has a squared-off twin. It is a switch in the browser rather than a second library, and it ships through the same doors the styles do.
0.4.0: Every sharp diagonal end is cut back to its round cap's box, on 329 icons: the chevrons, arrowheads, signs and slashes that painted 0.414 outside their rounded siblings sit on the same box now, and every arc the converter had bent by moving its endpoint is a true arc again. settings-dot's sharp gear is cut on its cap's own line, so its grey plate ends flush with the black instead of escaping past it, and circle-navigation sits centred in its box.
0.5.0: Two names changed hands: the diagonal chain is link now and the horizontal one link-2, which is the naming the rest of the set already follows, and link-off became link-2-off with it, so an import of either wants updating. Four sharp drawings that painted outside their rounded siblings were re-solved rather than exempted, and the formatting marks moved onto a Text shelf of their own.
unreleased: The seven currency marks arrive with circled halves, and those hold 1 unit of daylight against the ring rather than the 2 the guide asks between elements: a container is the frame a drawing sits in, not a neighbour it has to be told apart from, and at 2 a letterform comes out at about half the well. Bitcoin has no circled half, because its four stubs stand outside the letter at both ends and solving them shrinks the B until its bowls carry 1 unit of white instead of 2.
